cases.prompt: The tree says opportunities created times win rate should equal opportunities won, but it's off by 18%. Is the data broken?
cases.setup: Win rate is the close-date figure. Opportunities created is a cohort count.
expect_pass: identifies the cause as a cohort mismatch rather than a data quality problem
states that the product edge is an identity only when the win rate is the created-cohort rate over the same cohort
recomputes with the created-cohort win rate and reports the new residual
notes that the created cohort must have matured or the recomputed rate is a lower bound and the edge will still not close
reports the residual as a number rather than as pass or fail
expect_fail: attributes the gap to data quality and recommends a pipeline investigation
adjusts one node to force reconciliation
declares an 18% residual acceptable

cases.prompt: New plus expansion plus renewal comes to 104% of revenue. Where's the extra 4%?
cases.setup: Upsells to existing customers are sometimes booked as new-logo opportunities, so they appear under both new and expansion.
expect_pass: identifies a partition failure on the filter edge rather than a summing error
names the specific overlap: upsells booked as new-logo opportunities appearing under two children
gives the diagnostic: list rows matching more than one child's filter and count them
states that the children must partition, so every revenue row belongs to exactly one, and proposes the rule that achieves it
notes the opposite possibility, that children can sum correctly while overlapping if an offsetting gap exists, so the partition check is separate from the sum check
expect_fail: scales the children down to sum to 100%
reports the discrepancy without identifying the overlap mechanism

cases.prompt: Build the demand funnel branch. We don't track sales-accepted leads.
cases.setup: No SAL event exists in the CRM. Every other funnel stage is instrumented.
expect_pass: keeps the SAL node in the tree marked unmeasurable rather than pruning it
records what instrumentation would make it measurable, specifically a lead status value or a task type logged on acceptance
records the consequence: MQL to SQL blends rejected and never-worked leads, which have opposite fixes
excludes the node from the arithmetic while leaving it visible, so the reconciliation is not distorted
assigns an owner to the gap
expect_fail: drops the node from the tree
estimates SAL from available fields and treats it as measured
leaves the node in the arithmetic, breaking the reconciliation

cases.prompt: Add NPS under retention so we can see how much of retention it explains.
cases.setup: NPS is a survey score. Retention is a rate on the revenue base.
expect_pass: adds NPS as a driver-of edge, not a product, sum or ratio edge
states that driver edges are excluded from every reconciliation check because they are not arithmetic
explains that mixing a driver edge into a product produces numbers nobody can reproduce
offers what can honestly be shown: the historical relationship between the two series, labelled as correlation with its lag
notes that survey response bias makes NPS a property of respondents, not of the base
expect_fail: creates a product or ratio edge from NPS to retention
reports a share of retention explained by NPS from an uncontrolled comparison
refuses to include NPS in the tree at all

cases.prompt: Here's our exec dashboard: revenue, bookings, win rate, ACV, NRR, churn. Good?
cases.setup: All six are lagging indicators. Pipeline created, meetings held and trial starts are available but not on the dashboard.
expect_pass: labels each existing tile lead or lag and states that all six are lagging
explains the consequence concretely: the dashboard confirms what already happened and cannot steer anything this quarter
proposes at least one leading node per branch from the metrics actually available
applies the test for a leading label: does the node historically move before its parent, at a lag consistent with the cycle, and says the label is asserted where this cannot be checked
keeps the tile count within a range an exec audience will actually read
expect_fail: approves the dashboard as-is
adds leading indicators without checking they lead
proposes a long list of additional tiles

cases.prompt: Build the tree with revenue at the top. Finance says 12.4M, the CRM says 13.1M.
cases.setup: The two systems have not been reconciled. The difference has been known for two quarters.
expect_pass: states that a tree built on a disputed top node propagates the dispute into every branch
builds the structure anyway, since the formulas and edges do not depend on which figure is right
leaves the top node's value open with both figures shown and the 700k difference named
routes the reconciliation itself to the appropriate work rather than guessing which system is right
names the likely causes worth checking first, such as bookings versus recognised revenue, currency conversion, and records excluded by one system's filters
expect_fail: picks one figure without stating why
averages the two
refuses to build any part of the tree until the dispute is settled

cases.prompt: We put pipeline velocity under revenue as a child. It doesn't reconcile.
cases.setup: Pipeline velocity is (opportunities × win rate × deal value) ÷ cycle length. Revenue is currency per period.
expect_pass: runs the dimensional check and reports that velocity's units are currency per unit time, not currency
states that velocity is therefore not a child of a currency node under any arithmetic edge
proposes the correct placement: velocity as a derived diagnostic, with its three numerator factors placed under revenue as a genuine product edge
notes that velocity is routinely mislabelled as a duration
notes that all four of its inputs must come from the same cohort and segment or the figure describes no team
expect_fail: keeps velocity as an arithmetic child and adjusts a tolerance to make it pass
describes pipeline velocity as a duration
removes velocity from the analysis entirely
